gold.summary: A historical policy edit keeps invalidating implementer selections made after that edit.

findings.title: Preserve implementers escalated after a policy edit
findings.detail: changedCells permanently marks edited cells, so this check suppresses every subsequent sticky target outside their chains—even targets selected by escalation after the edit. The engine supplies only the saved preference on ordinary feedback rounds, so routing returns to the weaker, previously failed model. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-CoMb3F/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-CoMb3F/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-CoMb3F/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-CoMb3F/claude-501/routing-review.test.ts. Assertion output: Expected: "claude/opus"; Received: "claude/sonnet-5.5". Result: 0 pass, 1 fail. The same routing sequence without a runtime edit retains Opus.
findings.failure_scenario: Set implement.small to ["claude/sonnet-5.5"]. After failed rounds, route with minTier: 5 and exclude: ["claude/sonnet-5.5"], selecting claude/opus. Without any further policy edit, the next feedback round passes prefer: "claude/opus" and incorrectly selects claude/sonnet-5.5.

findings.title: Removed sticky implementers return after a daemon restart
findings.detail: Sticky-target removal depends on the process-local changedCells set. After resetting an operator override, startup constructs the Router with the restored base policy, so setPolicy sees no difference and changedCells stays empty. A resumed run's saved implementer is then appended and pinned even though the reset removed it from the effective cell. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-LYIf8g/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-LYIf8g/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-LYIf8g/claude-501 bun -e 'import { Router } from "./src/router/router.ts"; import { ProviderTracker } from "./src/router/providers.ts"; import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { DEFAULT_POLICY, PROVIDERS } from "./src/
findings.failure_scenario: A run uses claude/opus from an operator override. The operator resets its cell to codex/sol, then the daemon restarts before the run's next implementation round. The resumed run selects the removed claude/opus again.

findings.title: Preserve stickiness for implementers escalated after an edit
findings.detail: changedCells permanently marks edited cells, so this check suppresses every subsequent out-of-chain sticky implementer, including stronger models selected by escalation after the edit. The next feedback round supplies only prefer and therefore returns to the weaker chain instead of retaining the escalated model. Reproduced with `bun test "$TMPDIR/routing-escalation-review.test.ts"`: `Expected: "claude/opus"; Received: "codex/luna"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Set implement.small to ["codex/luna", "codex/sol"], then escalate with minTier: 5 and both chain entries excluded. The router selects claude/opus. With no further edit, the next round using prefer: "claude/opus" selects codex/luna.
